articles.title: AMCH becomes Northeast India's first centre to administer enzyme replacement therapy for ...
articles.content: News Assam AMCH becomes Northeast India’s first centre to administer enzyme replacement therapy for lysosomal storage disease AMCH becomes Northeast India’s first centre to administer enzyme replacement therapy for lysosomal storage disease Assam Medical College and Hospital (AMCH), Dibrugarh, has achieved a significant milestone in specialised healthcare by successfully administering Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT) to a three-and-a-half-year-old child diagnosed with a lysosomal storage disease (LSD). Advertisement India TodayNE Sep 05, 2026 , Updated Sep 05, 2026, 3:14 PM IST Follow us: Assam Medical College and Hospital (AMCH), Dibrugarh, has achieved a significant milestone in specialised healthcare by successfully administering Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT) to a three-and-a-half-year-old child diagnosed with a lysosomal storage disease (LSD). According to information released by the institution, the therapy was administered using Velaglucerase alfa, making AMCH the first centre in Northeast India to successfully provide this specialised treatment for an LSD patient. The procedure was conducted under the leadership of Dr Arpita Gogoi of the Department of Paediatrics, with support from a multidisciplinary team of doctors and specialists at AMCH. The treatment was delivered through the medical college’s Centre of Excellence for Rare Diseases, established by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, under the National Policy for Rare Diseases, 2021. Lysosomal storage diseases are a group of rare genetic and metabolic disorders that can require specialised diagnostic facilities, long-term clinical management and disease-specific therapies. Access to such treatments can be particularly challenging for patients in regions where specialised rare disease services are limited. The successful administration of ERT at AMCH marks an expansion of the hospital’s capabilities in the diagnosis and management of rare diseases and provides access to advanced treatment for patients from Assam and other parts of the Northeast. The development also highlights the growing role of specialised public healthcare institutions in extending rare disease services beyond major metropolitan centres. The availability of enzyme replacement therapy at AMCH could help reduce the need for patients and their families to seek specialised treatment outside the region. With the successful treatment, AMCH’s Centre of Excellence for Rare Diseases is expected to further strengthen its capacity to manage patients with rare genetic and metabolic conditions and facilitate access to specialised therapies in the Northeast. articles.title: Ananth Technologies supplied electronics for ISRO's GSLV-F17 and EOS-05 - NewsBytes
articles.content: Ananth Technologies supplied electronics for ISRO's GSLV-F17 and EOS-05 Technology Sep 04, 2026 Ananth Technologies, based in Hyderabad, played a major behind-the-scenes role in ISRO's recent GSLV-F17 rocket launch and India's first imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit, EOS-05. They provided key electronics and subsystems that kept both missions running smoothly. Ananth working on Gaganyaan and Aditya-L1 For GSLV-F17, Ananth supplied 28 crucial packages for things like power management and command systems, plus handled testing and integration of important rocket parts. On the EOS-05 satellite side, they delivered 15 critical systems, including tech for power conversion and onboard computing. With advanced facilities in Bengaluru and Thiruvananthapuram, Ananth is now working on even bigger projects like Gaganyaan (India's human spaceflight) and Aditya-L1 (solar mission). Their chairman says it best: "Our involvement across launch vehicle electronics, stage integration and testing, as well as power, onboard computing and attitude sensor systems for the spacecraft, reflects our growing end-to-end capabilities in the Indian space ecosystem."

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh Governor, CM congratulate ISRO scientists - english.punjabkesari.com
articles.content: Andhra Pradesh Governor, CM congratulate ISRO scientists By: IANS On: Friday, September 4, 2026 6:53 PM Google News Follow Us Amaravati, Sep 4 (IANS) Andhra Pradesh Governor S. Abdul Nazeer and Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Friday congratulated the ISRO scientists on the successful launch of GSLV-F17. The Governor congratulated ISRO scientists for achieving a significant milestone with the successful launch and placing in geosynchronous orbit, its heaviest Earth observation satellite, EOS-05, via the GSLV-F17 rocket from Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota on Friday. The Governor said the mission marks India’s acquisition of its first dedicated imaging satellite, crucial for continuous surveillance and national security & it adds another feather in ISRO’s cap. Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu described it as a proud moment for India’s space journey. “Congratulations to ISRO on the successful launch of GSLV-F17 and the precise placement of EOS-05 into its intended orbit. This remarkable achievement reflects the strength of India’s space capabilities and the dedication of our scientists and engineers. My best wishes to the entire ISRO team for many more milestones ahead,” the Chief Minister said in a post on X. Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan termed the launch a new milestone in Bharat’s space journey from Earth to the stars. “Bharat continues to push the boundaries of what is possible. The successful GSLV-F17 mission, placing EOS-05 into its intended Sub-Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit, marks another remarkable achievement for ISRO. EOS-05 is India’s first-ever imaging satellite from a geosynchronous orbit, strengthening our Earth observation capabilities. Heartiest congratulations to the brilliant ISRO scientists, engineers, technicians and everyone involved in this historic mission,” said Pawan Kalyan, who is also the minister for science and technology. Pawan Kalyan stated that under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India’s space programme continues to reach new heights, inspiring our youth and strengthening our position among the world’s leading spacefaring nations. Former Chief Minister and YSR Congress Party President Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy also congratulated ISRO on the successful GSLVF17 launch carrying EOS05 from Sriharikota. “I commend the scientists and engineers whose dedication and precision made this achievement possible. The mission strengthens weather monitoring, disaster management and national development, inspiring immense pride in India’s expanding space capabilities and progress,” he said. –IANS ms/uk (This content is sourced from a syndicated feed and is published as received. articles.title: ISRO successfully launches Earth observation satellite EOS-05 - Manorama Yearbook
articles.content: • Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully launched the country’s first ever imaging satellite in the Geosynchronous orbit on September 4. • A Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) rocket, carrying Earth observation satellite EOS-05, lifted off from the second launch pad at Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota in a pre-dawn mission. • The satellite was successfully placed in the intended sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit, about 18 minutes after it lifted off from the spaceport. • While several earth observation satellites operate from Low Earth Orbit (LEO), the EOS-5 satellite is set to hover at an altitude of roughly 36,000 km above earth, which is the geosynchronous orbit and at that level, the satellite will match Earth’s rotational speed. • At over 2,300 kg, this is the heaviest satellite ever to be carried by a GSLV. • This was the 107th launch from Srihariharikota and the 19th mission of GSLV. • Once the EOS-05 is operationalised, it will become India’s first dedicated imaging satellite to monitor the Earth from geosynchronous orbit, about 36,000 km above the Earth. (The author is a trainer for Civil Services aspirants.)

articles.title: PM Modi hails ISRO's GSLV-F17 launch carrying EOS-05 as proud moment for India - Sikkimexpress
articles.content: TODAY is Saturday, September 5,2026 21.71° c Saturday, Sep 05, 2026 23:00 [IST] Last Update: Friday, Sep 04, 2026 17:27 [IST] NEW DELHI, (IANS): Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday congratulated the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) on the successful launch of the GSLV-F17 rocket carrying the EOS-05 Earth observation satellite, describing the achievement as a matter of national pride. PM Modi took to his social media 'X' and said, "Yet another outstanding achievement by ISRO and a proud moment for our nation. The successful launch of GSLV-F17 carrying EOS-05, India’s first-ever imaging satellite from Geosynchronous orbit is a reflection of the excellence, innovation and growing capabilities that define India’s space sector." "The growing partnership between ISRO and Indian industry is adding new strength and scale to our space programme and expanding India’s capabilities across the entire space ecosystem," he said. The GSLV-F17 rocket lifted off successfully from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh, at 2:55 a.m. IST on Friday in a pre-dawn launch. The EOS-05 satellite was subsequently placed into its designated sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit. ISRO Chairman Dr V Narayanan expressed satisfaction over the mission’s outcome, saying the GSLV-F17 had precisely injected the advanced Earth observation satellite into its intended orbit. Mission Director Thomas Kurian described the achievement as a significant milestone for the GSLV programme. He said the mission marked the 19th flight of the GSLV and carried a specially configured Earth observation satellite capable of providing near-real-time imaging. Kurian also pointed out that EOS-05 is the heaviest satellite that the GSLV has placed into a geosynchronous transfer orbit or sub-GTO orbit. He credited the successful launch to years of extensive preparation and dedicated efforts by scientists, engineers and other teams involved in the mission. The EOS-05 mission is designed to strengthen India’s Earth observation capabilities. The satellite is expected to provide a continuous view of the country from an altitude of nearly 36,000 km above the Earth, supporting advanced imaging and observation applications. The GSLV-F17 launch vehicle is 51.7 metres tall and has a liftoff mass of approximately 420.5 tonnes, making it one of India’s major operational launch systems. Science and Technology Minister Jitendra Singh also welcomed the successful mission, stating that India’s space programme continues to achieve new milestones and reinforce the country’s standing as a major global space power. "EOS-05 is a state-of-the-art Earth Observation satellite and India's first imaging satellite from geosynchronous orbit, enabling advanced imaging across visible, infrared, multispectral and hyperspectral bands," Jitendra Singh wrote on X.

A beaming ISRO chief V Narayanan said: "I am very happy to announce that the GSLV F-17 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the advanced EOS-05 geo imaging satellite in the intended and required orbit." "The health of satellite is perfectly alright," he said. "This is a great achievement for our country's space programme because this is the first EOS that will be placed on the geo platform for the national activities." In the days to come, the orbit raising maneuvering will be done and the satellite will be elevated to required orbit and will be placed in the geo platform, he said, adding the success is the culmination of team work of ISRO and its industrial partners. articles.title: ISRO all set for state-of-art imaging satellite launch - Nagaland Post
articles.content: Infotainment ISRO all set for state-of-art imaging satellite launch ISRO all set for state-of-art imaging satellite launch September 4, 2026 ISRO has commenced the countdown for the launch of a state-of-the-art Earth observation spacecraft on Friday, which will be India’s first ever imaging satellite from the Geosynchronous orbit, official sources said. The 27-hour countdown started at 23.30 hours on Wednesday for the GSLV-F17/EOS-05 mission and the 51.7 metre tall rocket is set to lift off at the appointed time of 2.55 AM on September 4 from the second launch pad at Satish Dhawan Space Centre, about 135 km from Chennai. GSLV-F17 is the 19th flight of India’s Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV), ISRO said. The scheduled Friday pre-dawn launch is following a gap of nearly 8 months. On January 12 this year, ISRO’s PSLV-C62 rocket carrying 16 satellites failed to place them in the intended orbit after encountering an “anomaly” in the critical third stage of the launch. This was ISRO’s only launch this year and it failed. A similar, previous attempt in May 2025 (PSLV-C61-EOS-09) also did not succeed due to a “motor pressure issue,” and there was a fall in the chamber pressure of the motor case. articles.title: ISRO launches India's first -ever 'Eye in the Sky' - The New Indian Express
articles.content: BENGALURU: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) created history in the wee hours of Friday by successfully launching the advanced Earth Observation Satellite (EOS)-05 into a geo-orbit, recording a first in placing an imaging satellite in a high-altitude orbit of 36,000 km altitude. This successful launch comes as major relief for the Geostationary Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) programme following the unsuccessful EOS-03 (GSLV-F10) mission in 2021, and also after the two failed missions of PSLV-C61/EOS-09 in January 2026 and PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 in May 2025. The EOS-05 satellite has been placed in a geosynchronous orbit above the South Asian landmass, which means it will remain stationary in relation to the location above which it has been parked in space, synchronising its revolution around Earth in tandem with the rotation of the planet. The 2,367-kg satellite – the heaviest that GSLV Mark II has put in space so far – was launched on board the GSLV Mk II-F17 mission (GSLV-F17) at 2.55 am from the second launchpad of Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC) at Sriharikota amid light rainfall. After the orbit-raising operations are completed, the satellite is to be placed above the South Asian land mass at an inclination of 19.28 degrees to the equator. This was the 107th launch from SDSC Sriharikota and the 19th of the GSLV. Once operational, EOS-05 will become India’s first dedicated imaging satellite from the geo-orbit, providing “strategic data” for the country, ISRO Chairman V Narayanan said after the launch, while describing EOS-05 as a “strategic satellite”. Satellite to provide real-time data for weather monitoring The satellite will give real-time data for weather monitoring, fast-moving disaster events like cyclones, floods and cloudbursts, agriculture assessments. Unlike low-Earth orbit observation satellites that pass over a location at regular intervals, EOS-05 is synchronous with Earth’s rotation to enable it an almost-constant watch over the Indian landmass. The satellite carries multi-spectral and hyper-spectral bands to capture selected field images every five minutes and the entire country every 30 minutes. Narayanan said the satellite’s assured mission life is seven years. “But I am confident that this will work effectively for more than nine years,” he told. “This was a very important mission for the country for continuously monitoring India and its nearby places for Earth observation for various applications. It has advanced cameras and important payloads. EOS-05 will also be used for other Earth observation purposes,” he said. He however, did not specify what he meant by “other purposes”. He, however, dismissed speculations that it was a “spy satellite”. Project Director (Satellite) Imteyaz Ahamad described EOS-05 as one-of-its-kind satellite with the multi-band operating capabilities. “The configuration is different,” he said. Dinesh Kumar Singh, Director, UR Rao Satellite Centre (URSC), said, “There is no morning better than this when we have just launched an ‘Eye in the Sky’. The spacecraft is in good health. All the initial operations have been successful.” Loud cheers erupted among Indian space scientists at 3.01am, after the GSLV MKII’s third stage cryogenic upper stage engine separation began and...

articles.title: PM Modi, Rajnath Singh Hail Successful EOS-05 Launch - Northlines
articles.content: Facebook X Pinterest WhatsApp NEW DELHI, Sep 4: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Friday hailed the successful launch of ISRO’s GSLV-F17 carrying EOS-05, describing the mission as a major achievement that strengthens India’s space capabilities and Earth-observation programme. Prime Minister Modi, in a social media post, congratulated ISRO on the successful launch of India’s first-ever imaging satellite intended for a Geosynchronous orbit . He said the achievement reflected the excellence, innovation and growing capabilities that define the country’s space sector. Modi also highlighted the expanding partnership between ISRO and Indian industry, saying it was adding new strength and scale to India’s space programme and broadening the country’s capabilities across the entire space ecosystem. The Prime Minister described the successful mission as an outstanding achievement by ISRO and a proud moment for the nation. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh also congratulated ISRO on the successful launch of GSLV-F17 carrying EOS-05. Singh said the satellite would strengthen India’s Earth-observation capabilities and reflected the growing sophistication of the country’s space programme. He said the expanding partnership between ISRO and Indian industry was providing greater scale to innovation, strengthening indigenous capabilities and opening new frontiers for India’s space ambitions. The Defence Minister further said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India was steadily building a progressive, self-reliant and globally competitive space ecosystem. The successful launch comes as a significant boost to India’s space programme, with greater cooperation between ISRO and domestic industry expected to further strengthen the country’s capabilities across the space sector. (Agencies)

EOS-05 imaging satellite launched On 4 September, the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully launched the EOS-05 imaging satellite at 2:55 pm. EOS-05 is India’s first satellite capable of taking images from a geosynchronous orbit, at an altitude of around 36,000 km. It was launched from Sriharikota aboard the GSLV-F17 rocket and will be able to continuously capture images of India and large surrounding areas. EOS-05 is India’s first satellite to carry out imaging from a geosynchronous orbit. It will continuously monitor borders and strategic areas, including the Pakistan-China border. It will also help monitor disasters and provide early warnings. GSLV-F17 is the 19th flight of India’s Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle. Through this mission, EOS-05 was placed in a sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit. ISRO launched a mission after around eight months. articles.content: Home Trending News ISRO successfully places EOS-05 satellite, India’s first-ever imaging satellite from Geosynchronous Orbit ISRO successfully places EOS-05 satellite, India’s first-ever imaging satellite from Geosynchronous Orbit ISRO has successfully launched the GSLV-F17/EOS-05 mission from the Second Launch Pad at Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Andhra Pradesh today. By Ishita Ganguly 04 Sep 2026 Follow Us New Update ISRO places EOS-05 satellite The Indian Space Research Organisation ( ISRO ) has successfully launched the GSLV-F17/EOS-05 mission from the Second Launch Pad at Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Andhra Pradesh on Friday (September 4). ISRO places EOS-05 satellite Seconds after blastoff from the Second Launch Pad, the GSLV-F17 vehicle surged upward. It met every critical flight parameter before placing the EOS-05 Earth observation spacecraft into its targeted Sub-Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit. EOS-05 is the heaviest GSLV ever launched and will become India’s first dedicated imaging satellite to operate from geosynchronous orbit once it reaches its operational orbit. Most Earth observation satellites operate from low Earth orbit (LEO), typically hundreds of kilometres above the planet. Advertisment Add Startup Pedia As A Trusted Source However, the EOS-05 satellite was injected into a sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit after Friday’s launch. It will use its own propulsion system to reach its required operational orbit at roughly 36,000 km above Earth. Following the precise orbital insertion, ISRO confirmed that "GSLV-F17 has successfully accomplished its mission, placing EOS-05 into the intended orbit." Key features of the spacecraft: Orbit: Sub-Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (targeting a permanent geosynchronous position). Primary Function: Advanced Earth observation and high-resolution imaging. Strategic Value: Provides continuous data streams critical for disaster management, environmental tracking, meteorological studies, and national security applications. India tried an Earth-observing satellite to GEO once in August 2021, when a GSLV Mark II launched the EOS-03 spacecraft. However, the rocket experienced an anomaly with its third stage, and the satellite was lost. Today's liftoff was the third orbital mission for India in 2026. The others were flown by ISRO's Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, which failed to deliver 16 satellites to orbit in January, and Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-1 rocket, which aced India's first-ever private orbital launch in July. Following today’s successful launch, ISRO chairman V Narayanan said, “I am very happy to announce that the Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV)-F17 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the advanced Earth observation satellite EOS-05, the Geo-Imaging Satellite, into the intended and required orbit [Sub-Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit].” Union minister Jitendra Singh said it was a "historic" launch, and that EOS-05 will enable advanced imaging across visible, infrared, multi-spectral and hyperspectral bands. Prime Minister Narendra Modi lauded it as “another outstanding achievement by ISRO and a proud moment for our nation.” He said, “The growing partnership between ISRO and Indian industry is adding new strength and scale to our space programme and expanding India’s capabilities across the entire space ecosystem.” Another giant leap for India in Space! articles.content: Punjab Newsline | Jalandhar In a major breakthrough against organised international crime and fugitives, Jalandhar Commissionerate Police have arrested Manjit Singh Bedi, a wanted fugitive allegedly involved in a high-profile fraud case linked to the US government’s Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). According to police, Bedi allegedly carried out a multi-million-dollar fraud under the US food assistance program before fleeing to India via Canada in April 2026 to evade law enforcement. SNAP provides food and nutritional assistance to economically vulnerable families in the United States. Bedi is accused of large-scale financial fraud and manipulation of the program and had reportedly been placed on the list of wanted fraud suspects by US investigative agencies. The arrest marks a significant achievement for Punjab Police in tackling transnational organised crime and fugitives. The action also highlights the increasing coordination between law enforcement agencies in tracking suspects who attempt to evade arrest by crossing international borders. articles.title: India's Geothermal Strategy Targets Power, Heating and Reuse of Abandoned Oil Wells
articles.content: Key Details The government’s overview, Geothermal Energy: A New Chapter in India’s Clean Energy Journey , brings together India’s resource estimates, policy framework and initial demonstration activity. Area Current position National framework The National Policy on Geothermal Energy , notified in September 2025, is implemented by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Estimated potential Approximately 10.6 GW , based on theoretical geothermal prospects Mapped resources 381 hot springs , ten geothermal provinces and 42 promising sites identified by the Geological Survey of India Puga Valley Two 1,000-metre wells commissioned by the ONGC Energy Centre in July 2026 for reservoir evaluation Proposed power project The Puga wells are expected to support a 1 MW demonstration geothermal plant Research programme MNRE sanctioned five R&D projects in July–August 2025 covering power generation, heating, cooling, resource assessment and indigenous technology Wider applications Direct heating and cooling, agriculture, aquaculture, ground-source heat pumps and possible reuse of abandoned oil and gas wells Government Overview Connects Policy with Early Field Activity The National Policy on Geothermal Energy, 2025 seeks to move India from mapping underground heat resources towards testing practical applications. It covers exploration, drilling, reservoir management, power generation and the direct use of geothermal heat. The policy also supports a national geothermal data repository, pilot projects and Centres of Excellence , alongside participation by government institutions, research organisations and private firms. Cooperation with Australia, Iceland and Saudi Arabia has identified geothermal energy as an area for research and knowledge exchange. Puga Is an Early Test of the National Strategy The ONGC Energy Centre commissioned two geothermal wells in Puga Valley, Ladakh, in July 2026 . Each well extends approximately 1,000 metres underground and will support an assessment of the geothermal reservoir. The wells are not a functioning power plant. They are intended to establish whether underground temperature, fluid availability and reservoir conditions can support India’s proposed 1 MW demonstration project . Puga is among the country’s most promising geothermal locations, but the demonstration remains an evaluation of technical performance rather than evidence that large-scale geothermal electricity is already commercially viable. Geothermal Could Supply Power When Solar and Wind Cannot Geothermal energy uses heat stored beneath the Earth’s surface. At suitable sites, underground hot water or steam can be brought to the surface to generate electricity. Its principal advantage is availability: unlike solar and wind, geothermal energy can potentially provide continuous, weather-independent output . This could make it a useful complement to variable renewable generation. Geothermal resources do not need to be hot enough to produce electricity to have economic value. Lower-temperature resources can potentially support: heating and cooling ; agricultural and greenhouse applications; aquaculture ; district or space heating; and ground-source heat-pump systems. Policy Extends Beyond New Geothermal Fields One strand of the national policy concerns abandoned or unproductive oil and gas wells . Subject to technical feasibility, such wells could be examined for geothermal applications using existing geological information, drilling expertise and infrastructure. The policy also recognises Enhanced Geothermal Systems and Advanced Geothermal Systems...

articles.title: Vice President congratulates ISRO on successful GSLV-F17/EOS-05 launch - The News Mill
articles.content: ANI Photo | Vice President congratulates ISRO on successful GSLV-F17/EOS-05 launch Vice President CP Radhakrishnan has congratulated the scientists and engineers of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) on the successful launch of the GSLV-F17/EOS-05 mission from Sriharikota, describing it as a significant milestone in India’s space journey. The Vice President called the successful injection of EOS-05, India’s first imaging satellite intended for placement in geosynchronous orbit, a major achievement for the country’s space programme. He termed it a “proud moment for Bharat” and another remarkable milestone for India’s space efforts. ADVERTISEMENT Stay connected Make The News Mill your preferred source See more TNM stories when you search for news on Google. Add TNM on Google In a post on X, he wrote: “Congratulations to the scientists and engineers of ISRO on the successful launch of the GSLV-F17/EOS-05 mission from Sriharikota today. The successful injection of EOS-05, India’s first-ever imaging satellite from geosynchronous orbit, marks a significant milestone in India’s space journey. A proud moment for Bharat and another remarkable achievement for India’s space programme!” Earlier, Prime Minister Narendra Modi also praised the successful launch, calling it an “outstanding achievement” and a proud moment for the nation. In a post on X, Modi said the mission reflected the “excellence, innovation and growing capabilities” of India’s space sector. ADVERTISEMENT The Prime Minister highlighted the growing collaboration between ISRO and Indian industry, stating that this partnership was strengthening and scaling up the country’s space programme and expanding capabilities across the wider space ecosystem. The EOS-05 Earth observation satellite was successfully deployed in the geosynchronous orbit from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota. The launch took place from the Second Launch Pad at the centre and was carried out by a GSLV-F17 rocket, the 19th flight of India’s Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle. The rocket carried EOS-05 to a Sub-Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (Sub-GTO). The mission attracted significant public interest, with students, teachers and space enthusiasts gathering at Sriharikota to witness the launch. Despite rain, many remained at the launch-viewing area eager to see the rocket lift off. ADVERTISEMENT EOS-05 is a state-of-the-art Earth observation spacecraft and is notable for being India’s first imaging satellite designed for placement in a geosynchronous orbit. From this orbit, the satellite is expected to provide repeated observations of large areas of the Earth and deliver information related to weather and agricultural updates, among other data. The mission also marks an important milestone for the GSLV programme, which is designed to launch heavier spacecraft towards geosynchronous orbits. The previous GSLV mission, GSLV-F16, successfully launched the NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) satellite in July 2025. articles.content: Cong hails launch of India’s imaging satellite By - Team MP Update: 2026-09-04 18:39 GMT New Delh,: The Congress on Friday hailed ISRO for the successful launch of the country’s first-ever imaging satellite in geo-orbit and accused the Modi government of undertaking a “radical role reconfiguration” that will “change the very character” of the Indian space agency. Friday’s launch marked the space agency’s maiden success for the year 2026. In a post on X, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said, “Congratulations to the entire @isro team on the successful GSLV-F17/EOS-05 mission! EOS-05, India’s first imaging satellite, from Geosynchronous orbit, will further strengthen our Earth Observation capabilities that we have been developing for years.” “We are immensely proud of our scientists, space engineers and researchers whose dedication and ingenuity continue to take India’s space programme to greater heights,” the Congress chief said. The Congress party has always remained deeply committed to scientific temper and space research, he said.

articles.title: India's First 'Sentient' Corporate Campus to Come in Pune - Deccan Chronicle
articles.content: Mumbai: India’s first sentient corporate campus will be set up at Bajaj FinservCampus at Koregaon Park Annexe, Pune. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Friday laid the foundation stone for the project. Speaking at the ceremony, CM Fadnavis said that the Bajaj Finserv Campus will not only be the largest but also the most intelligent and sustainable ecosystem in the country. Built with AI and IOT at its core, the Bajaj FinservCampus building will sense its environment and occupants’ needs and proactively adapt in real time. According to company sources, the AI and IoT systems will enable the Campus to respond to changing weather, occupancy and environmental conditions. Sensors and analytics will help optimise energy and water consumption, crowd density and movement. Predictive maintenance systems using IoT sensors will monitor critical infrastructure, while automation and robotics will support Campus operations. The Campus’ eco-efficient design will maximise natural breeze and daylight while reducing cooling requirements. The Campus will operate on renewable energy and target 80% water recycling, rainwater harvesting and zero waste. It’s biophilic design will bring nature into the workplace through extensive green zones, including rare Ayurvedic gardens, Miyawaki and replanted native forests. Native species from Maharashtra will be used to support biodiversity. The Campus will be supported by floor and cluster-level monitoring of air quality and temperature. An integrated employee app will provide access to campus facilities, including navigation, parking and bookings. The Campus will also have an integrated medical centre offering telemedicine and emergency response services, along with dedicated wellness support. Sanjiv Bajaj, Chairman & Managing Director, Bajaj Finserv, said, “Built to global LEED and IGBC standards, the Campus will combine eco-efficient and biophilic designs with AI-driven systems and operate entirely on renewable energy. The Campus will be a testament to a tech-ready future and to India’s growing financial and technological strength.”
